title: Proportional KV Cache Allocation and Pipe-Aware Scheduling for Multi-GPU Inference
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a proportional KV cache allocation algorithm and pipeline-aware scheduling layer to optimize multi-GPU memory utilization for continuous-batching inference. The goal is to reduce token-level memory pressure and tail latency variance when models are served across mixed tensor/pipeline parallel topologies. Deliverables: design doc, prototype scheduler integrated with runtime, microbenchmarks showing memory and latency improvements, and a rollout plan for Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime can compute per-device proportional KV allocations based on live sequence length distribution and pipeline stage weights; 2) Eviction/prefetch policy integrates with allocation so hot-key replication is supported; 3) End-to-end benchmark shows >=8% latency tail (p95) reduction or >=10% reduction in max GPU memory headroom across representative workloads; 4) No regressions in throughput for short-sequence scenarios; 5) Feature flag gated and has telemetry (per-GPU kv occupancy, eviction rate, prefetch hits) in Console.
design_notes: Core idea: track rolling histograms of sequence length and per-stage effective KV working set; compute a proportional share of global KV capacity per GPU, then realize it with a two-layer mapping: (a) a stable slice assignment for cold slabs, (b) a dynamic hot-slab overlay that can replicate top-k hot keys onto neighboring devices when stage affinity requires it. Scheduler uses pipeline-aware affinity scores to prefer placing hot overlays on devices that will see the keys sooner in the forward pass, minimizing cross-stage NVLink traffic. We will reuse existing KV metadata schema (compact slab ids) and extend it with an allocation epoch token to allow safe in-flight migrations.
tradeoffs:
- Proportional allocation reduces fragmentation but adds compute to allocation decisions; we mitigate by amortizing decisions to allocation epochs (1000s of requests).
- Hot-key replication reduces remote fetch latency at the cost of extra memory and replication bandwidth; we limit replication footprint via an LRU-guided budget and a configurable replication factor.
- Migrations can cause transient increased PCIe/NVLink traffic; we schedule migrations during low-util windows and support backpressure if network saturates.
benchmarks: Prototype microbenchmarks on rtx-a6000 and p4d: initial runs show 9% p95 latency reduction on mixed-traffic chat workload and 12% reduction in maximum per-GPU free memory variance. Synthetic hot-key workload shows prefetch hit rate improvement from 67% to 89% with a 5% memory replication budget. Full-scale cluster tests pending; see linked artifacts.

comments: 2026-03-12: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to prioritize a proportional algorithm over hard partitioning after seeing fragmentation in 8-GPU tensor+pipe jobs.
2026-03-13: Prototype allocation controller implemented; discovered per-stage weight estimation is noisy for very bursty traffic. Decided to use EWMA with percentile clipping to stabilize weights.

2026-03-13: Benchmarks: mixed chat workload (seq 8-1024) ran on 4xA100-40GB cluster; p95 latency down ~9% and memory headroom variance improved. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2124 (WIP)

2026-03-14: Design review feedback from Research: add formal correctness notes for migration epoch token and ensure backward compatibility with existing slab format. Action: update design doc and add unit tests for epoch transitions.

2026-03-14: Blocker: on machines without NVLink, replication bandwidth causes measurable throughput drop in synthetic long-seq test. Plan: feature-gate replication to only enable on NVLink-topologies for initial rollout and add a NIC/PCIe throughput check in autoscaler.
Next steps: harden migration safety, add eviction metrics to telemetry, and coordinate with Dedicated rollout owners for staged enablement.
